body.statement: Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise implies the positive correcting-move property on the matching-component graph class, but the converse fails even for smooth identifiable ANMs. For all sufficiently small \(\sigma>0\), \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(6)\): symmetry gives \(\rho^{\leftarrow}_{12}=0\), while \(\rho^{\to}_{12}\to1\) and both directional ratios on edges \(3\to4\) and \(5\to6\) converge to \(1\). Nevertheless, for \(\pi_1=(2,3,4,5,6,1)\) and \(\pi_2=(1,2,4,6,3,5)\), \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_1)=1<2=\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_2)\), whereas \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_1)\to2\) and \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_2)\to1+4/5+5/6>2\). Continuity of the correlation ratios, together with forward residual independence and Condition 19 reverse dependence for every \(\sigma>0\), makes the reversed ranking strict for small positive \(\sigma\). Thus Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) guarantees local recovery for a support-closed smooth law excluded by Li et al.'s premise.
body.justification: An explicit score-limit calculation certifies a strict reduction in the recovery hypothesis, rather than a verbal comparison between differently named conditions.
body.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3 and its proof on page 5) establish sufficiency of global reversal monotonicity but do not separate it from the local property their optimizer needs.
body.consumer: Users obtain a guarantee for heterogeneous modular systems whose inversion costs cannot be ranked by an unweighted reversal count.
